question: Do the public ASEANO outputs for the Imus River watershed provide fish species or waterbody-specific occurrence evidence, and what additional fish-related leads do the proceedings identify?

sourceReviews.title: ASEANO Project Report: Mapping and Characterization of the Imus River Watershed
sourceReviews.provider: PEMSEA; ASEANO project; Cavite State University

findings.scope: The official report page describes watershed boundary delineation and mapping, topography, stream characteristics, geomorphology, political subdivisions, barangay/population distribution, land cover, and hydroclimatic analysis.
findings.reportedNetworkContext: The page reports a drainage area of 11,259.80 ha, 56 perennial streams with a combined reported length of 186.15 km, and 36 river segments. These are source-reported watershed/network summaries, not a channel geometry or a fishing-area boundary.
findings.fishEvidence: Searchable report text contains no fish checklist, fish-survey method, fish station, or species result. A map legend mentions a fish pond as a land-use class; that is not biological fish evidence.
findings.geometryAndReuse: The report describes DEM-based watershed delineation, but no item-specific reuse license or ready-to-use vector boundary was verified. Do not copy the report map or infer fishing reach geometry from the watershed outline.

sourceReviews.title: End of Project Stakeholders’ Forum on the Results of the ASEAN-Norwegian Cooperation Project on Local Capacity Building for Reducing Plastic Pollution in the ASEAN Region (ASEANO Project)
sourceReviews.provider: PEMSEA; Provincial Government Environment and Natural Resources Office, Cavite

findings.publicOutputCrossCheck: The proceedings summarize the watershed-mapping and plastic-pollution components and state that detailed project reports and studies were available for dissemination; they do not establish that every related project deliverable is present in the proceedings.
findings.fishTissueLead: During discussion, the proceedings report that CvSU said microplastics research in fish tissues had been conducted in Bacoor and that results could be shared with interested participants. The proceedings do not identify taxa, exact collection site/waterbody, dates, sampling method, study title, dataset, or voucher identifiers.
findings.localityAndIdentity: The generic Bacoor locality does not resolve the lead to Imus River, Bacoor Bay, or a particular site. The proceedings do not establish whether this fish-tissue lead is the same study as previously documented Bacoor shell/bivalve microplastics work.

sourceReviews.title: CAFENR faculty and researchers participate in ASEANO
sourceReviews.provider: Cavite State University, Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension

findings.presentationCrossCheck: The newsletter says CvSU presented the Imus River watershed mapping/characterization subproject and a separate plastic-waste sources/concentration subproject at the July 6, 2022 end-project forum.
findings.fishEvidence: The newsletter summary contains no fish taxa, fish-sampling method, waterbody-specific fish observation, or fish dataset.

sourceReviews.title: Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed

findings.reconciliation: The public PEMSEA mapping report is a watershed-mapping product presented under ASEANO. The reviewed sources do not prove that it is the full final deliverable for the broader CvSU Research Center project listing.
findings.period: The Research Center listing and the January 2021 CvSU newsletter give different end dates; no reviewed final report resolves the discrepancy.

reconciliation.projectIdentity: The public watershed-mapping report and CvSU forum/newsletter summaries are associated with the Imus ASEANO work, but they do not establish that the mapping report is the complete final report for the broader biophysical-characterization project.
reconciliation.speciesEvidence: No species-level fish evidence for Imus River was found in these materials. The forum’s Bacoor fish-tissue remark is an unresolved study lead, not a named taxon, occurrence record, or site assignment.
reconciliation.boundary: The reported watershed area and stream-network length are not a verified river channel, validated fishing-area geometry, or legal boundary. Existing source-specific length measurements remain unreconciled.
reconciliation.period: The CvSU project listing and planning newsletter still differ on the project end date; do not choose one without the final report.

rightsReview.decision: Retain bibliographic metadata and short factual findings only. Do not reuse report maps, figures, GIS files, newsletter images/prose, or fish-tissue data without item-specific rights review.

limitations: The report PDF text was searched, but the report is a watershed mapping and characterization product; an absence of species in reviewed/report-indexed content is not proof that no fish work occurred elsewhere in the broader project.
The forum records only a brief oral discussion of microplastics research in fish tissues in Bacoor; no study document or identifying metadata was located in this review.
The forum remark does not establish that the tissue study examined a finfish species or that specimens came from Imus River or Bacoor Bay.
No item-specific reuse rights for the mapping report or forum/newsletter material were established.
nextAction: Search for the referenced CvSU Bacoor fish-tissue microplastics study using official CvSU and collaborating-institution records. Verify the study identity, taxa, exact waterbody/site, sampling dates and methods, vouchers, and reuse terms. Keep it separate from published Bacoor Bay shell/bivalve studies unless a source explicitly links them. Separately continue seeking the broader Imus vulnerability/pollution deliverables and retain the project-date discrepancy.
